prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: השוואת דירות להשכרה בתל אביב (language he, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "שכונה" · longest unbreakable word 65px · one-line width 86px
  col 2: header "מחיר" · longest unbreakable word 42px · one-line width 102px
  col 3: header "חדרים" · longest unbreakable word 42px · one-line width 42px
  col 4: header "קומה" · longest unbreakable word 42px · one-line width 138px
  col 5: header "הערות" · longest unbreakable word 79px · one-line width 1064px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Rendering convention: the screenshot always shows the WHOLE table. Anything beyond the dashed box is not clipped; it is the part a reader reaches by scrolling sideways, so judge both what fits in the box at first sight and the cost of scrolling to the rest.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"להשוות בין דירות להשכרה בתל אביב לפי שכונה, מחיר, מספר חדרים, קומה והערות.","reading":"הקוראים סורקים מימין לשמאל כדי לזהות שכונה, להשוות מחיר וחדרים, ואז לבדוק קומה והערות לכל דירה. גובה שורה שנוצר מהערה ארוכה יכול להכיל גם גלישה טבעית בתאים אחרים באותה שורה.","groups":["שכונה מזהה כל דירה ומשמשת עוגן לקריאת השורה.","מחיר וחדרים הם נתונים עיקריים להשוואה וצריכים להיות קלים לסריקה יחד.","קומה והערות מספקות פרטים משלימים שעשויים להשפיע על הבחירה."],"keep_intact":["שמות השכונות ומילים בודדות ככל האפשר","מספרי מחירים, מספרי חדרים ומספרי קומות"],"may_wrap":["הערות בין מילים","תיאורי קומה בין מילים","מחיר ויחידת הזמן בשורות נפרדות"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [107, 90, 63, 90, 180] · table 531×1069px · row heights [36, 153, 176, 176, 153, 176, 199] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 171px
Design r1B: widths [107, 90, 63, 99, 160] · table 520×1231px · row heights [36, 176, 199, 199, 199, 199, 222] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 9 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 160px
Design r1C: widths [107, 90, 63, 63, 150] · table 474×1301px · row heights [36, 199, 199, 199, 222, 199, 246] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 10 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 114px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
